origin: Manual mode keeps the settled lane on one screen, and the screen carries a way out of it: say discuss and a number and that finding is pulled aside after the rest land, for an exchange that can end in the finding not landing at all. This walks the gated screen end to end — two settled calls on one screen, one documented with the rest and one talked through and declined for cause, with the reason on the row — and then the gated cycle end, where the re-loop gate asks before a follow-up round rather than taking one.
conduct: The user is resuming their card-payments specification to run its review; construction finished last sitting, so offered the resume choice they continue. The review puts a two-row screen of calls made on their behalf to them — the missing 30-day refund window and a rounding rule for partial refund amounts — each with what it rests on named beside it, offering to document the screen, to hand every remaining call over automatically, to pull one out and talk about it, or to expand one. They never hand anything over automatically: they want to see what goes into the specification. The refund window they are happy with — the discussion decided it. The rounding rule they are not, and they want to talk about that one: their gateway's refund API only accepts integer minor units, so a fractional amount cannot reach it and the rule would specify a case the system cannot produce. They want it left out, and they say so with that reason. Asked whether to run another review round, they proceed to completion — one finding landed, one was declined for cause, another cycle is not owed. At sign-off they confirm. Throughout they answer concretely and never reopen what they settled.
